prerequisites: parallel attendance of Technische Mechanik 2 and Werkstofftechnik/-Prüfung

learning_outcomes.text: Students can characterize the functionality of the machine elements covered.

They understand the functional, geometric, and other requirements and dependencies between individual machine elements and other connecting components, in relation to their operating and constructional contexts.
They can select suitable machine elements for applications within the conception and design of assemblies. In doing so, they are also sensitized to sustainability aspects.
They are familiar with the basic types of stress underlying standardized calculations and can design their own components adapted to stress and manufacturing requirements.

They master the differentiation between design calculations and verification calculations for various operating conditions and can independently set up and perform these calculations in a simplified analytical way for most of the machine elements covered, while adhering to valid standards.
They are familiar with researching required equations and data using the textbook and possibly other documents.
They can methodically work on a simple development task in a small group under accompanying coaching, discuss technically and result-oriented, and organize themselves in a team.

syllabus_topics: Elementary overarching design principles: Simple, Clear, Safe; 4 phases.
Qualitative design principles / rules (force flow, deformations, stresses, notches, manufacturing, assembly).
Basic stresses and deformations of simple components with symmetrical cross-sections (quantitative).
Consideration of sustainability aspects (material utilization, reduction of processing steps, waste avoidance, etc.) in design and detailed planning.
Types of connections (fixed, movable, elastic; separable/non-separable; form/force/material fit).
Movable connections: Pins/plain bearings, motion screws, guides, rolling bearings.

Axles and shafts with modeling and simplified design and verification calculations for tough steels (with notch effect and design factors, but without mean stress influence and load collectives, only statically and against fatigue fracture).
teaching_methods: Project task in small groups with coaching (determining the lecture topics, compulsory meetings with presentations and homework in group and/or individual work)
assessment_rules: The examination form will be announced at the beginning of the lecture. Successful completion of the module examination is required to obtain credit points. Study achievement (SL) is required for module completion.
